What does zone X mean?

Zone X is outside the high-risk zones. Federal rules use it for two kinds of land: areas of moderate flood hazard, and areas of minimal hazard (44 CFR §64.3). FEMA's map shows the moderate kind shaded and the minimal kind unshaded.

Am I required to buy flood insurance?

Federal law requires it only in a high-risk zone (A or V) with a federally regulated or backed mortgage, or federal help to buy or build (42 U.S.C. §4012a). Outside them, a lender can still require it.

What does it cost in zone X, by state?

Since FEMA's Risk Rating 2.0, price is set from each building's own flood risk, not its zone, and these are existing policies whose buildings differ. The reason for any one zone is not in this data.

Does zone X flood?

Yes. The last column of the table above shows, state by state, the share of NFIP claim dollars paid on claims rated outside zones A and V, in every year on record. That is every zone other than A and V, not zone X alone. It uses the zone on each claim, not today's map, and leaves out claims with no zone. That share is not a chance of flooding for any one home.

How do I get covered?

Most policies start 30 days after you buy, but there is no wait if you buy it with a new or refinanced mortgage. To buy: call the NFIP at (877) 336-2627, go to FloodSmart.gov, or ask any licensed insurance agent. Every NFIP insurer offers the same rates.

What this page cannot tell you

Your premium, private insurers' prices, your exact zone, why prices rise, and whether a home is in the shaded or unshaded part of zone X, because policy records do not separate them. FEMA's map and an agent's quote answer those for your address.
